chunks: Abdul Wahid ibn Muhammad ibn Abdos al-Attar (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Qutayba al-Naysaboori quoted on the authority of Hamdan ibn Soleiman al-Naysaboori, who said: 'I asked Al-Ridha (peace be upon him) about the words of God, the Exalted: “Those whom God wills to guide, He opens their breasts to Islam…”'

He (the Imam) said: 'Those whom God wishes to guide in their faith in this world to His Paradise and the House of His Honor in the Hereafter, He opens their breasts to submission to God, trust in Him, and calmness regarding the rewards He has promised, until they find peace in Him.'

And those whom He wishes to leave astray from His Paradise and the House of His Honor in the Hereafter, due to their disbelief in Him and disobedience to Him in this world, He makes their breasts narrow and constricted, so that they doubt their disbelief, and their hearts become unsettled because of it, until they become as if they were ascending to the sky.
Thus does God place the penalty (or impurity) upon those who do not believe.
ai.seo_question: How does God open or constrict the human heart according to Shia interpretation of Surah Az-Zumar?
ai.summary: In this tradition from *Uyun Akhbar al-Rida*, Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) elucidates the divine mechanism of *fath* (opening) and *shadd* (constriction) of the breast as described in Surah Az-Zumar. He distinguishes the spiritual tranquility and certainty granted to the guided from the inner turmoil and doubt afflicting the misguided, linking these psychological states directly to their ultimate eternal destiny. This interpretation underscores the Shia understanding of divine decree (*al-Jabr wa al-Tafwid*) as a manifestation of God's will based on the individual's inherent disposition and actions.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 11-27 Abdul Wahid Muhammad ibn Ubdoos al-Neishaboori al-Attar - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Qutayba al-Neishaboori quoted on the authority of Hamdan ibn Soleiman al-Neishaboori, “I asked Al-Ridha about the Honorable the Exalted God’s words, ‘Those whom God (in His plan) willeth to guide, He openeth their breasts to Islam…’

The Imam (s) said, ‘Those whom God wishes to guide in their faith in this world towards Paradise and His House of Munificence in the Hereafter, He will open their breasts to submit to God, rely on Him, get calmed by the rewards that He has promised until they trust Him. But regarding ‘…those whom He willeth to leave straying…’

to be deprived of His Paradise and His Home of His Munificence in the Hereafter due to their disbelief in it and their disobedience of God in this world. ‘…He maketh their breast close and constricted…’  so that they fall in doubt in his state of disbelief.
God will upset their belief in their heart as things get so hard for them ‘…as if they had to climb up to the skies: thus doth God (heap) the penalty on those who refuse to believe.’”
